newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank meet not about money policy.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank meet not about money policy.

text.p: A scheduled October 19 meeting of Taiwan's central bank will have "nothing to do" with adjustment of monetary policy, vice governor Liang Cheng-chin said on Friday.
The main agenda item at the meeting will be reform of banks' reserve system, Liang told reporters.
"It will have nothing to do with adjusting monetary policy," Liang said. "(The market) should not think too much about this."
Liang noted that current interbank money rates were low and foreign exchange rates were stable, implying that there was no need to adjust Taiwan's monetary policy.
"There is no need to say further if we need to adjust monetary policy," he added.
Liang declined to further clarify the bank's intentions on monetary policy.
Liang's boss, central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong, has said regularly in October that the central bank would maintain an "appropriately loose" monetary policy.

Sheu said on October 7 that liquidity had become "slightly too loose" but that the bank would maintain appropriate looseness without letting interest rates drop "too low so as not to hurt the interests of most depositors."
Sheu said that the bank's loose monetary policy had shown itself not to be a "cure-all" for Taiwan's slowing economy.
Sheu noted that five consecutive decreases in commercial banks' reserve requirements since mid-1995 had made money more accessible but had failed to reignite private investment.
Further liberalisation was needed to bring unregulated or illegal financing operations into legal channels.
It was not known whether the October 19 meeting would take up proposals for such liberalisation.
The bank has said the meeting would review a proposal to set a direction to lower banks' reserve requirements and at the same time raise the liquidity ratio.
